title: Scientific opinion on the extension of the authorisation of use of the food additive steviol glycosides (E 960a–d) and the modification of the acceptable daily intake (ADI) for steviol
authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Flavourings (FAF), Castle L, Andreassen M, Aquilina G, Bastos ML, Boon P, et al.
funder: European Food Safety Authority; requestor: European Commission (question number EFSA-Q-2023-00594), following an application to extend uses and modify the ADI. Adopted 25 September 2024.
result: Steviol glycosides from stevia (E 960a) are obtained by water extraction of the leaves of Stevia rebaudiana Bertoni and contain not less than 95% steviolbioside, rubusoside, dulcoside A, stevioside and rebaudiosides A, B, C, D, E, F and M. Steviol glycosides are not hydrolysed by digestive enzymes of the upper gastrointestinal tract; colonic microbiota release the aglycone steviol, which is absorbed and glucuronidated, and steviol glucuronide is excreted in urine and partly via bile into faeces. In eight men given rebaudioside A or stevioside, steviol glucuronide in urine accounted for 59% and 62% of the doses. The Panel found insufficient justification to raise the ADI of 4 mg/kg bw per day, expressed as steviol equivalents, to 6 or 16 mg/kg bw per day.
